skill.name: pricing-reference-frames
skill.description: Design the reference-frame stack for pricing copy. Picks the strongest plausible anchor (inertia / opportunity cost / replacement cost / competitor) for the operator's PSP segment, generates the anchor copy block, and applies Prospect Theory loss-aversion patterns so the page reads "worth it or refund" rather than "save 40%." Loaded by the main pricing skill when the operator asks about anchoring, framing, or rewriting pricing copy.
skill.summary: Choose a credible pricing anchor and draft quantified, loss-aware copy with a bounded outcome guarantee.
skill.author: cmj-hub

content.value_statement: Pricing copy can emphasize competitor discounts instead of the buyer's actual costs. This skill selects a credible reference frame and drafts quantified copy with bounded guarantees.
actual_capabilities: Gather customer segment, current pricing, and optional competitor inputs from brand configuration.
Ask for current tools, labor costs, time spent, and consequences of delaying a solution.
Choose among status quo, opportunity cost, replacement cost, and competitor reference frames.
Draft a headline, quantified subhead, three mechanism bullets, and a bounded outcome guarantee.
Rewrite gain-focused claims using loss-aversion language.
Explain rejected frames and check copy for unsupported anchors and disallowed pricing patterns.
limitations: Requires operator evidence for customer costs and outcomes; it does not independently verify those claims.
Provides writing guidance, not conversion experiments, market research, or guaranteed revenue improvements.
Configured as a routed sub-skill, not a directly user-invocable command.
References shared pricing documents and a sibling sub-skill that are not included in this single-file package.

use_cases.title: Position a SaaS pricing page
use_cases.description: Compare current tools and manual work against the product, then draft an anchor above the pricing tiers.

use_cases.title: Rewrite segment-specific copy
use_cases.description: Select an evidence-backed frame for one customer segment and replace discount-led messaging with quantified outcome language.

use_cases.title: Explain internal replacement costs
use_cases.description: Use supplied staffing and maintenance estimates to explain the alternative to purchasing, with a bounded guarantee draft.

prompt_templates.title: Identify a starting anchor
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a pricing reference frame for [product] and [customer segment]. Ask about current tools, time spent, and costs before drafting.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: discover the evidence needed for a pricing anchor.

prompt_templates.title: Draft the anchor block
prompt_templates.prompt: For [segment], current work takes [hours/week] at [hourly cost], plus [monthly tool costs]. Our price is [price]. Draft the anchor block. Use only supplied facts. Ask for approved guarantee terms.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: turn supplied customer costs into pricing copy.

prompt_templates.title: Rewrite and compare frames
prompt_templates.prompt: Rewrite this pricing copy: [copy]. Use these verified customer costs and outcomes: [evidence]. Compare all four frames, explain rejected choices, and show loss-aversion changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: revise existing copy and document the rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Develop segment-specific recommendations
prompt_templates.prompt: Using supplied customer segments, current tiers, and cost evidence, recommend a frame for each segment. Draft separate blocks within the skill's word limits. Explain rejected frames and flag evidence gaps. Use only these approved guarantee terms: [terms].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: prepare multiple recommendations with explicit evidence and guarantee constraints.

output_examples.input: Founders spend six hours weekly on manual reporting. Our service costs $199 monthly and automates collection. Approved guarantee: first-month refund if setup exceeds 30 days.
output: Chosen frame: Status quo. The verified anchor is six hours of manual work each week.
Headline: Stop spending six hours a week collecting reports.
Subhead: Replace manual collection with automated reporting for $199 monthly.
Mechanism: Automate collection. Reduce repetitive work. Deliver consolidated reports.
Guarantee: If setup exceeds 30 days, we refund your first month.
Rejected frames: No opportunity, replacement, or competitor cost evidence was supplied.

output_examples.input: A procurement team estimates $120,000 to build internally and $20,000 yearly maintenance. Subscription costs $12,000 yearly. No guarantee is approved.
output: Chosen frame: Replacement cost, based on the supplied internal build and maintenance estimates.
Subhead: Compare your build estimate and $20,000 annual maintenance against a $12,000 yearly subscription.
Evidence gap: Confirm comparable scope before publishing the cost comparison.
Guarantee: Pending approved outcome, deadline, and liability terms.
Rejected frames: Current workflow and delay costs were not quantified.

best_practices: Start with one customer segment and verify its current workflow, labor rates, tool costs, and measurement period.
Choose the strongest plausible frame, and keep every numerical claim tied to supplied evidence.
Approve guarantee outcomes, deadlines, and liability limits before publishing the generated copy.
anti_patterns: Inventing customer costs or urgency to make an anchor appear stronger.
Leading with competitor discounts when a credible status quo or replacement frame exists.
Publishing an open-ended guarantee or an outcome commitment the business cannot deliver.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a reference-frame recommendation, an anchor copy block, rejected-frame explanations, and a summary of loss-aversion changes.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Tool compatibility does not establish that shared dependencies are included.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide a customer segment, current pricing, current workflow costs, and relevant outcome evidence. Competitor information is optional.

faq.question: Can I invoke it directly?
faq.answer: Its metadata marks it as not user-invocable. The main pricing skill routes anchoring and pricing-copy requests to it.

faq.question: Does it verify savings or conversion improvements?
faq.answer: No. It uses supplied evidence and flags missing quantification. Verify claims and test copy before making performance commitments.

faq.question: Are additional references required?
faq.answer: It references shared pricing guidance and a sibling tier-design sub-skill. Those files are not included in the audited single-file package.
